title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, choosing the right foods is crucial to ensure the health and well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy, helping to build a balanced and safe diet.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
The following international pantry staples are good for pregnancy:
- Oats: rich in fiber, supporting digestive health and reducing the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, supporting the development of bones and teeth for the baby.
- Lentils: rich in protein, fiber, and iron, supporting the development of the fetus.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, supporting the development of the brain and eyes for the baby.
- Eggs: rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals, supporting the development of the fetus.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, supporting the immune system and reducing the risk of disease.

## Building Balanced Plates
To build a balanced and safe diet, pregnant women should combine these international pantry staples with each other. Here are some suggestions:
- Breakfast: oats with Greek yogurt and fruit.
- Lunch: salad with leafy greens, lentils, eggs, and low-mercury salmon.
- Dinner: soup with leafy greens, lentils, and chicken or beef.

## Food Safety During Pregnancy
When pregnant, ensuring food safety is crucial to reduce the risk of disease and protect the health of both mother and baby. Here are some tips:
- Choose fresh and clean food.
- Cook food thoroughly before eating.
- Avoid eating raw or undercooked food.
- Avoid eating food that contains mercury or other toxic substances.

## Conclusion
International pantry staples can help build a balanced and safe diet for pregnancy. Pregnant women should combine these staples with each other and ensure food safety to reduce the risk of disease and protect the health of both mother and baby. For more information on [pregnancy meal planning](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner), visit our website.

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about your diet during pregnancy, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian for advice and support.
